title: Research: reviving an author session on another machine
body:
**Intent:** answer backlog item 15's open risk by experiment. Can an author's Claude Code session be revived on another machine, at another path, so a reviewer can still ask it questions?

**Headline:** it works, with no path rewrite. A transcript forks from any file, in any checkout, using Docent's exact read-only options. Subagent transcripts need three fields changed first. Slimming a snapshot to user and assistant records removes most personal data by itself, and cut an Opus fork of PR #43's session from $1.16 to $0.73. Priming a snapshot once let later questions read the prompt cache ($0.018 per question down to about $0.002 on Haiku), which bears on item 23.

**Behavior change:** none. One new research doc: `docs/research/2026-11-11-session-snapshots.md`.

**Tier:** 1. Docs only, but it sets direction for the snapshot format and scrubbing, so it gets a fresh-context review.

**Evidence:** 16 forks against two of this project's own transcripts, copied to a scratch folder (originals checksummed, unchanged). "Another machine" was a fresh clone at PR #43's head under a different path. Total model spend about $2.01. `pnpm verify` passes.

**Look here first:** the "What we checked" table, and "Recommendation for item 15".

**Known gaps:** same user, login and Claude Code version throughout; a separate `~/.claude` couldn't be logged in. One PR, four questions, one or two runs per variant. The primer result is Haiku only. The scrubbing inventory uses home-made gitleaks-style patterns, and the doc gives kinds and counts only.
